newsitem.title: USA: NYSE June 9-13 program trading averages 14.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: NYSE June 9-13 program trading averages 14.3 pct.

text.p: The New York Stock Exchange said program trading for the week of June 9-13 amounted to 14.3 percent, or 76.7 million shares a day of the exchange's average daily volume of 537.4 million shares.
In the previous week, such trading volume accounted for 14.8 percent of average daily volume, or 70.5 million shares a day.
The exchange said buy programs accounted for 9.5 percent, and sell programs accounted for the remaining 4.8 percent of the average daily volume of program trades.
In all markets, program trading averaged 117.8 million shares a day during the week beginning June 9.

Of the five member firms reporting the most program activity on the NYSE, BNP Securities, Natwest and Salomon Bros each executed all or most of their program activity for customers, as agent or facilitator.
Morgan Stanley and Lehman Bros executed most of their program trading activity as prinipal, for their own accouts.

Program trading executed by firms as agent, for non-member customers, amounted to 66.8 percent during the week, while volume executed as principal, for their own accounts, amounted to 30.1 percent of program volume from June 9-13.
In the same week, 20.9 percent of program trading volume executed by NYSE member firms was related to index arbitrage, while another 1.9 percent involved other derivative product-related strategies.
Program trading encompasses trading strategies involving the sale or purchase of a basket of at least 15 stocks with a value of $1 million or more the exchange said.
